channel.title: DevPulse · Inference
channel.description: Daily inference stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: Muse Spark Open reaches 36 tokens per second across four Mac Studios with MLX
item.description: Apple reports over 36 tokens per second for the nearly trillion-parameter Muse Spark Open on four Mac Studios, using MLX and RDMA over Thunderbolt at an 8,192-token context. The setup offers a concrete reference for distributed inference on unified-memory hardware.

item.title: PS5LM serves GGUF models from a jailbroken PS5 using llama.cpp
item.description: PS5LM runs llama.cpp's Vulkan backend on the PS5 GPU, uses 11.4 GB of shared memory, and exposes OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs to devices on the network. It is a concrete edge-inference deployment, though tied to jailbroken console hardware.

item.title: MJev-Spatial replaces spatial answer generation with one-pass classification
item.description: MJev-Spatial scores candidate answers using pretrained query and key projections, handling choices, numeric values, and points without generating answer tokens. A single forward pass for each decision could reduce latency in spatial tasks that require frequent interaction.

item.title: Beam serving on Google Cloud reports up to 5× higher performance and 8× lower latency
item.description: Google Cloud and Reflection report up to 5× higher performance and 8× lower latency for Beam using llm-d with vLLM or NVIDIA Dynamo with SGLang. The serving recipes and reported gains are relevant to teams running large models for agent workloads.

item.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark brings local coding agents and model customization to one PC
item.description: RTX Spark pairs a GB10 system-on-chip with up to 128GB of unified memory for running coding agents, fine-tuning models, and deploying locally. A single-machine setup could simplify local agent development and testing.

item.title: Speculative Forcing stops denoising tokens once their outputs are stable
item.description: Speculative Forcing accepts tokens early when a verifier judges their intermediate estimates sufficiently close to final outputs, while retaining their cached keys and values. It reports matching the four-step LongLive generator with about 1.7 denoising steps, a promising route to cheaper video generation.

item.title: Velox routes video-world attention by spatial memory and speeds chunk 48 denoising 2.43×
item.description: Velox uses camera-frustum overlap to select historical context, reporting 4.36× faster attention and 2.43× faster denoising at chunk 48. The approach targets growing KV-cache costs in long interactive video rollouts.

item.title: ExecuTorch runs TinyML models on Cortex-M with under 90 KiB of RAM
item.description: The Cortex-M backend runs four MLPerf Tiny models on an Alif Ensemble E8 in 21.5 ms or less, using under 90 KiB of RAM; the core runtime is under 20 KiB of flash. This shows a single PyTorch workflow can reach tightly constrained devices without a framework conversion step.

item.title: KV4-RL protects selected KV positions to speed INT4 rollouts
item.description: KV4-RL keeps attention sinks and recent context in INT8 while quantizing the rest to INT4, achieving 1.80× cumulative rollout speedup and 1.27× full-iteration speedup with final accuracy within 0.5 percentage points of BF16. The results show how selective KV-cache protection can improve RL training throughput while limiting quality loss.

item.title: SageMaker JumpStart adds repeatable model deployment and performance testing
item.description: The guide deploys a pretrained model, runs a lightweight performance test with the SageMaker SDK and removes the endpoint afterward. Named endpoint configurations target low cost, low latency or general-purpose workloads.

item.title: DoSA skips unnecessary sparse-attention scores with exact selection guarantees
item.description: DoSA uses score bounds to avoid fully scoring candidates that cannot enter Top-K, reporting up to 2.74× Indexer speedup and up to 1.94× time-to-first-token speedup. Its exact-selection approach offers a concrete path to faster sparse-attention serving.

item.title: PyTorch Inductor replaces Spyre’s custom compiler stack with one 7× smaller
item.description: IBM moved Spyre’s torch.compile backend from a separately built stack to an Inductor backend, leaving most of Inductor unchanged and shrinking the compiler about 7×. It’s a concrete example of adapting a shared compiler to a non-GPU inference accelerator.

item.title: Pulse Local uses small on-device models to answer questions about spending
item.description: A tuned Qwen3 0.6B model turns spending questions into structured queries, code handles the arithmetic, and a 4B model checks answers, with disagreement prompting uncertainty. This is a concrete pattern for keeping sensitive data local while limiting model errors.

item.title: Indra OCR reports 49 pages per second on 32 CPU cores
item.description: Indra OCR pairs a 1M-parameter recognizer with layout boxes, labels and reading order, reporting 49 pages per second on 32 CPU cores and higher OmniParseBench scores than Tesseract and PP-OCR. Its CPU throughput and structured output may make document ingestion cheaper and easier to integrate.

item.title: Fused MoE kernels combine routing and expert computation into GPU operations
item.description: The post describes fused MoE operations that combine token routing, data shuffling, and expert computation, and discusses hardware-specific kernel optimizations. Efficient MoE kernels can directly affect inference latency and cost, though the excerpt gives no performance results.

item.title: A browser RAG demo retrieves four passages and summarizes them locally
item.description: The demo combines in-browser semantic search with a small language model that summarizes the four most relevant passages, and measures answer faithfulness. Local execution keeps typed questions on the user's machine; the excerpt does not give the measurement results.

item.title: Intel D270 offers up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X for inference
item.description: Intel describes a 350 W, air-cooled PCIe accelerator with up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X, aimed at long contexts and concurrent agent sessions. The specifications are relevant to inference capacity planning, though no independent performance results are provided.

item.title: ReplaySSM speeds hybrid-model decoding with checkpointed state and input buffers
item.description: ReplaySSM stores a checkpoint plus recent inputs, cutting state-memory traffic roughly in half and speeding decoding kernels 1.46–1.80x; speculative throughput rises 1.85–2.10x. The design targets memory traffic, rollback, and precision trade-offs in hybrid-model serving.

item.title: Janas streams model experts from SSD and reports 24 tok/s on a 48 GB model
item.description: On a 32 GB laptop, Janas reports 24 tok/s generating with a 48 GB Qwen3-Next-80B model, versus 2.8 tok/s for llama.cpp, and also reports faster prompt processing. The results could inform trade-offs for running models larger than available RAM.

item.title: An iPad app runs an unmodified Linux AMD GPU driver for on-device inference
item.description: The app bundles the upstream Linux amdgpu and amdkfd drivers in a PCIDriverKit extension, then runs its inference engine on an AMD GPU in a Thunderbolt enclosure. The design is a notable example of bringing GPU inference to an iPad.

item.title: DCOCO restores context across parallel speculative drafts
item.description: DCOCO keeps multiple draft-token candidates and checks their compatibility across positions in parallel, restoring context among draft tokens at low additional cost. Its throughput results across four verifier backbones and ten benchmarks make it relevant to speculative-decoding design.

item.title: Bedrock routes OpenAI GPT inference across Regions in five Asian markets
item.description: The guide configures global cross-Region inference for Bedrock-hosted GPT models and covers API calls, permissions, and monitoring. This offers serving teams a path around capacity limits in a single Region.

item.title: SageMaker serves llama.cpp decision models with probabilities over fixed choices
item.description: The guide uses llama.cpp on SageMaker for text generation and extends the runtime with SemIf to return probabilities over declared options without decoding an answer token. That pattern suits agent routing and other systems that need scores over actions rather than generated text.

item.title: LatentGRM cuts reward-judge inference time by up to 7x
item.description: LatentGRM compresses evaluation trajectories by 8.9–9.2x and reduces judge inference time by 6.1–7.0x at vote@5, with competitive preference accuracy against explicit SFT judges. It shows how rubric-guided latent reasoning can lower the cost of model evaluation.

item.title: PreSTO batches speculative proposals without changing PowerMH sampling
item.description: PreSTO batches prefetched Metropolis–Hastings proposals while preserving PowerMH's transition kernel, reporting median speedups of 1.71×, 1.91× and 2.33× across seven datasets and five base LLMs. The approach targets sequential sampling overhead without changing the sampler's behavior.

item.title: SoloQ enables calibration-free quantization for diffusion language models
item.description: SoloQ rotates weights and activations into a predictable distribution for data-independent low-bit quantization, and applies commit-time KV-cache quantization to block-diffusion models. Calibration-free deployment could simplify quantization where activations shift across denoising steps.

item.title: BetterWispr runs speech transcription locally on a Mac
item.description: The open-source dictation tool uses built-in models on the Mac, works offline after model downloads, and has no cloud fallback. It is a concrete example of local inference for a user-facing application, though the listing gives no performance details.

item.title: Fixed-choice decision models select an answer in one forward pass
item.description: The approach masks all but a fixed set of answer tokens and picks the highest-probability option in one pass, instead of generating a constrained response token by token. This can make structured, fixed-option answers faster to produce.

item.title: A corruption-lattice cost predicts the minimum steps for generative decoding
item.description: The paper models decoding schedules as paths on a corruption lattice and defines their cost by discarded dependence; for Markov data on a graph, zero-cost schedules require steps equal to the graph's treedepth. This offers a way to assess decoding schedules before running them.

item.title: SpecFold reuses shared computation across diffusion-model draft branches
item.description: SpecFold uses token-level residual gating to reuse parent attention and FFN computation across speculative branches, with a Triton kernel for sparse execution and reported throughput gains. The algorithm-system co-design targets a distinct source of inference cost in diffusion language models.

item.title: MC-Sparse reuses attention metadata to speed diffusion transformers without visible quality loss
item.description: MC-Sparse groups similar queries for GPU execution and caches selected KV tokens and dense-to-sparse residuals across denoising steps; experiments report better dense-attention fidelity and larger speedups than sparse baselines. Its training-free approach targets the latency and quality trade-off in long-sequence generation.

item.title: Apogee rebuilds Mozilla Orbit as a local, private browser summarizer
item.description: Apogee summarizes web pages and other content without sending or storing data, using Ollama, WebGPU or Transformers.js for local inference. It offers a concrete example of bringing AI summarization onto users' devices.

item.title: LittleBit-2 uses latent geometry alignment for sub-1-bit LLM compression
item.description: LittleBit factorizes weight matrices into binary latent factors with learned scales; LittleBit-2 adds latent rotation and iterative quantization before quantization-aware training. The released implementation gives inference engineers a concrete extreme-compression approach to evaluate.

item.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 targets high-volume workloads at 75% lower cost
item.description: Anthropic says Haiku 5.5 costs about 75% less to run than Haiku 4.5 and is designed for fast, repetitive tasks, including use as a coding subagent. The price and speed claims matter for teams balancing model capability against serving costs.

item.title: Whistle runs speech recognition on-device in a 16.9 MB model
item.description: Whistle is a 16.9 MB speech model that runs on CPU without dependencies, with transcription, word timestamps and speech embeddings across seven languages. Its compact local runtime is relevant to teams deploying speech features on constrained devices.

item.title: rGPU runs PyTorch workloads on a remote NVIDIA GPU
item.description: rGPU offers a PyTorch device interface and CUDA shims that let client applications run GPU work on a remote NVIDIA machine. The two integration paths could help teams use remote accelerators without rewriting existing workloads.

item.title: STEPQuant preserves recurrent-state accuracy at a nominal six-bit budget
item.description: STEPQuant assigns precision by error magnitude and memory lifetime, and fits scales to key-row and value-column effects; tests on Qwen3.8-27B and Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct report accuracy close to FP32 at a nominal 6-bit budget. This targets recurrent-state memory costs in concurrent serving.

item.title: GRACE compresses video latents while preserving compatibility with pretrained DiTs
item.description: GRACE retains a frozen base latent and learns a residual for information lost under stronger compression, while aligning compressed latents to the pretrained distribution. This targets faster video diffusion without requiring a DiT retrain.

item.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 matches Luna's price through 100,000 tokens
item.description: Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10/$0.50 per million input/output tokens up to 100,000 tokens, but uses about 1.25 times as many tokens for the same long prompt as Haiku 4.5. Above 100,000 tokens its price rises fivefold, making workload length important to serving cost.

item.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 arrives on Bedrock at a lower cost than Haiku 4.5
item.description: AWS says Haiku 5.5 is available on Bedrock and costs around 75% less than Haiku 4.5 for most tasks, with AWS IAM, audit and monitoring controls. The release is relevant to teams comparing model cost and deployment options.

item.title: OpenTPU runs modern models on an FPGA accelerator with bit-exact simulator output
item.description: OpenTPU runs ten models with real weights on a Kintex-7 FPGA and produces tokens matching its simulator bit for bit; the project reports decode and prefill throughput. Its end-to-end hardware, compiler, and software stack offers a concrete way to study inference accelerators.

item.title: Anthropic subscriptions may use over 40% of inference compute on 10% of revenue
item.description: The analysis estimates that subscriptions account for 10% of Anthropic revenue but over 40% of inference compute, lowering blended revenue per megawatt by about $36 million. Those estimates connect subscription design to serving demand and compute economics.

item.title: llama.cpp adds MTP decoding and new attention kernels in v0.6.0
item.description: The release adds MTP speculative decoding for Qwen4Exp, with a reported ~1.5× decode speedup on DGX Spark, plus Metal flash attention and sparse Vulkan attention. These changes offer concrete options for improving local inference performance.

item.title: LoHi improves long-video VLM accuracy by balancing frame resolution and coverage
item.description: LoHi combines dense low-resolution video with sparse high-resolution frames, improving average accuracy by 10.6 percentage points across three benchmarks; the study also finds front-end decoding dominates hour-long video wall time. This offers concrete guidance for trading visual detail against temporal coverage and latency.

item.title: RealtimeWAM overlaps video and action inference and generates actions in one step
item.description: RealtimeWAM combines one-step action generation, teacher-anchored consistency distillation, and asynchronous cross-expert pipelining with shared video KV cache. These techniques target iteration and waiting overheads in action-model inference.

item.title: Ollama defaults supported Apple Silicon models to MLX
item.description: On Apple Silicon, Ollama now runs supported model architectures on MLX by default and adds several models, including decision models. This changes the local inference runtime path for users of supported models.

item.title: GLM 5.3 becomes available as a managed model on Amazon Bedrock
item.description: The 753B-parameter mixture-of-experts model is available through managed APIs with cross-Region inference and prompt caching. Engineers can assess a managed serving option for coding and long-horizon agent tasks without operating the inference infrastructure themselves.

item.title: Qwen 125B runs locally at up to 94 tokens/s on tested consumer GPUs
item.description: Strata reports generation speeds of 53–94 tokens/s across quantizations on an RTX 5070 and an RX 9070 XT, with prompt processing also measured. Engineers weighing local inference can compare the speed and hardware trade-offs against server-based deployment.

item.title: vLLM 0.31.0 adds GPU optimizations and persistent weight caching
item.description: The release adds SM100 attention and KV-cache optimizations, fused operations, and a preload CLI that keeps post-quantized weights resident across engine restarts. These changes target inference performance and faster recovery of serving capacity.

item.title: SCM searches local photos and video frames with vision, OCR, and speech models
item.description: SCM indexes local media for semantic, scene, OCR, and spoken-dialogue searches, using local inference and background re-embedding. Its combined multimodal pipeline and offline design are useful patterns for engineers building private AI applications.

item.title: OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol is priced below Astra and posts reported benchmark gains
item.description: The roundup reports Sol pricing of $2/$10 per million input/output tokens, versus Astra at $10/$50, and claimed gains on DeepSWE v1.1 and AutomationBench. The cost and task-performance claims offer a useful comparison point for model selection.

item.title: Bedrock adds India geographic cross-Region inference for Claude models
item.description: Claude models are available through geographic cross-Region inference from Mumbai and Hyderabad, with requests processed in India Regions. The post explains the residency model and how to invoke it through Bedrock APIs.

item.title: HeteroFold transfers KV caches across model families without prefill
item.description: HeteroFold maps and calibrates a frozen sender's KV cache for a frozen receiver, handling differences in tokenization and model structure. At 32K context, one reported transfer is 10.7 times faster than native prefill and 1.18–1.47 times faster than prior prefill-free baselines.

item.title: Jev cuts edge-orchestration decision latency 22.7–64.5% versus LLMs
item.description: Across 8,280 requests and a live admission path, Jev reduces median decision latency versus the fastest LLM, with lower fees on four-field contracts but some exact-match loss. The comparison gives engineers concrete trade-offs when choosing models for latency-sensitive orchestration.

item.title: Google's Project Suncatcher prototype satellite reaches orbit
item.description: Google says its prototype satellite is in orbit and will test how TPUs withstand spaceflight, radiation and thermal extremes. The data could inform designs for future machine-learning infrastructure beyond Earth.

item.title: Parallel Power Tempering balances exploration and exploitation in LLM sampling
item.description: PPT runs interacting sampling replicas at different sharpening levels, letting lower-power chains explore while higher-power chains exploit likely responses. The work also addresses truncation bias and studies swap strategies under finite compute and memory budgets.
